Special Branch Reorganization Circular No. 7 - 7 - 30.

Duties of Japanese Members of Special Branch

While attached to Special Branch No. 2, it will be the duty of C.J.I. Nakagawa to collect information of interest to the Special Branch and, in addition, to render to the Crime Branch any assistance for which he is called upon or which he is in a position to give. His duties in .2 will be specifically as follows :-

1. To maintain contact with the managements of Japanese mills and collect any information which they are able to give on the subject of Red propaganda and labour agitation. In discharging this duty he should endeavour to obtain full information about :
(a) demands for higher wages or improvement in working conditions;
(b) complaints against foremen or others;
(c) strikes;
(d) efforts to influence workers by Red propaganda and formation of Red cells;
(e) opening of Red schools, etc.

2. To keep in touch with Japanese news agencies and other Japanese enterprises interested in happenings in the interior with a view to being in a position to obtain early details of any information they obtain of military or political movements in the interior which are of interest to the Settlement.

3. To maintain liaison with the Japanese Consulate, Japanese Landing Party, H.I.J.M.'s Navy and Japanese shipping companies so as to be in a position to convey to them quickly information on the subject of impending troubles in connection with which their assistance may be required, etc. and to collect any information of use to the Police which they are able to furnish.

4. To make inquiries when ordered to do so about Japanese individuals, Japanese enterprises, etc.

5. To watch and report on political movements among Japanese which are of interest to the Municipal Council or Police Force.

6. To watch and report on the movement and plans of Japanese Communists and persons of other nationalities of similar political beliefs who are associated with them.

7. To compile lists from time to time of Japanese Communists who either live in Shanghai or who visit this place from time to time.

8. To assist in the censoring of Japanese films intended for exhibition in Shanghai.

Information of the character mentioned in Nos. 2 and 3 should be immediately conveyed to Special Branch No. 2

特务科改组通告第7号 - 1930年7月7日。

特务科日籍成员之职责

中川（Nakagawa）首席日籍探员（C.J.I.）在隶属特务二科期间，其职责为收集对特务科具有价值的信息，此外，还应向刑事科提供其所被要求或力所能及的任何协助。其在二科的具体职责如下：-

1. 与日本纱厂管理层保持联系，收集其所能提供的关于赤色宣传及劳工煽动方面的任何信息。在履行此职责时，他应努力获取关于以下方面的完整信息：
(a) 提高工资或改善工作条件的要求；
(b) 对工头或其他人的投诉；
(c) 罢工；
(d) 通过赤色宣传和建立赤色小组来影响工人的企图；
(e) 开办赤色学校等。

2. 与日本通讯社及其他关注内地事态的日本企业保持联系，以便能够及时获取它们所掌握的、涉及租界利益的内地军事或政治动向的任何信息的详细情况。

3. 与日本领事馆、日本登陆部队、日本帝国海军及日本航运公司保持联络，以便能够迅速向其通报可能需要他们协助的即将发生的骚乱等相关信息，并收集他们所能提供的对警方有用的任何信息。

4. 奉命时对日本个人、日本企业等进行调查。

5. 监视并报告在日本人中发生的、对工部局或警务处具有利益关系的政治运动。

6. 监视并报告日本共产党人以及与其有联系的其他国籍持相同政治信念者的行动和计划。

7. 不时编制居住在上海或不定期来访上海的日本共产党人名单。

8. 协助审查拟在上海放映的日本电影。

上述第2和第3项所述性质的信息应立即报送至特务二科

The duties of Detective Sergeant Kim of Special Branch
No. 6 will until further orders be as follows :-

1. To obtain early information of plans of Koreans to hold
meetings, organise demonstrations or to start activities
aiming at the creation of disturbances or likely to lead
to disturbances.

2. To peruse all Japanese newspapers and periodicals carefully
and translate items objectionable in a moral or political
sense or otherwise of special interest to the Municipal
Council or Police

3. To translate when so required documents in Japanese received
by the Municipal Police or other departments of the S.M.C.

4. To obtain early information about new Japanese newspapers,
periodicals, etc. which contain undesirable matter,
especially articles hostile to the Municipal Council.

5. To trace Korean revolutionary literature in circulation in
Shanghai and make translations of important parts of it.

6. To keep a list of all Japanese and Korean newspapers and
periodicals published in Shanghai with particulars of
the address, circulation, name of editor, policy, etc. of
each publication.

7. To keep a list of all Japanese news agencies in Shanghai and
other parts of China and be in a position to furnish
information as to the owners, policy, etc. of these
enterprises.

8. To make inquiries regarding activities of Korean revolutionists
and persons of other nationalities associated with them.

9. To attend whenever required by the Crime Branch, Divisions
Branch or Traffic Branch for the purpose of translating
or interpreting from Korean into English and vice versa,
and to assist the Crime Branch and Traffic Branch in a
general way in making investigations into Korean cases.

10. To attend meetings convened by Koreans and report on the
proceedings at these gatherings.

11. To submit a report daily on the efforts now being made
to secure information about the movements and doings
of Korean undesirables.

J.R. Griers
Officer i/c Special Branch.

在接到进一步命令之前，隶属特务六科的警长金（Kim）的职责如下：-

1. 尽早获取朝鲜人计划举行集会、组织示威或开展旨在制造骚乱或可能导致骚乱的活动的信息。

2. 仔细审阅所有日本报纸和期刊，翻译在道德或政治意义上令人反感的内容，或对工部局或警方具有特殊兴趣的其他内容。

3. 根据需要，翻译公共租界警务处或工部局其他部门收到的日文文件。

4. 尽早获取包含不良内容的新办日本报纸、期刊等的信息，特别是那些对工部局持敌对态度的文章。

5. 追踪在上海流传的朝鲜革命文献，并翻译其中的重要部分。

6. 保存一份在上海出版的所有日本和朝鲜报纸及期刊的清单，并列明每份出版物的地址、发行量、编辑姓名、方针等详情。

7. 保存一份在上海及中国其他地区的日本通讯社清单，并能够随时提供有关这些企业的所有者、方针等信息。

8. 调查朝鲜革命者及与其有关联的其他国籍人士的活动。

9. 应刑事科、分区科或交通科的要求出席，目的是进行朝英互译，并在一般意义上协助刑事科和交通科调查涉及朝鲜人的案件。

10. 出席由朝鲜人召集的会议，并报告这些集会的进程。
正在进行
11. 每日提交一份报告，汇报目前为获取关于不受欢迎的朝鲜人的行踪和活动信息所做的努力。

格里尔斯（J.R. Griers）
特务科主管警官。

REPORT ON THE NATURE OF DUTIES PERFORMED BY J. D. I. NAKAGAWA.

Made by J. D. I. S. Nakagawa Forwarded by

Sir,

The work performed by the undersigned consists mainly of supervising the work of Japanese members of the C. I. D. when engaged in general investigation of crimes, such as trafficking in firearms, narcotic drugs, etc. common among Japanese. Monthly reports on the work of Japanese Detectives and crime in general, wherein Japanese interests are involved, are compiled and forwarded to the D. C. I. at the end of each month.

In pursuance of orders from the D. C. I., instruction classes are held every Friday at the office of the undersigned at the Central Station when instructions on methods of crime detection and other necessary subjects are delivered by the undersigned to the junior members.

Stations where Japanese Detectives are attached are visited by me from time to time when, apart from examining the diaries kept by Japanese Detectives, the Senior Detective i/c and the Superintendent, etc. are consulted for the purpose of establishing co-ordination of work and discipline among the detectives under my supervision.

In addition to making enquiries into cases on behalf of various sections of the department, such as the Political Section, Foreign Section, Chinese Section, Indian Section, Arms Section, etc., often entailing difficulty and responsibility, it is also part of the duty of the undersigned to act as liaison officer between the Shanghai Municipal Police and

关于日籍初级探员中川（J. D. I. NAKAGAWA）履行职责性质的报告。

由日籍初级探员 S. 中川（J. D. I. S. Nakagawa）呈报 转呈

阁下，

卑职所做的工作主要包括监督刑事侦缉处日籍成员在调查日本人中常见的犯罪（如枪支贩运、毒品贩运等）时的工作。每月末编制并向副刑事侦缉处长（D. C. I.）提交关于日籍探员工作及涉及日本利益的一般犯罪情况的月度报告。

根据副刑事侦缉处长的命令，每周五在中央捕房卑职办公室举办培训班，由卑职向初级成员讲授犯罪侦查方法及其他必要科目。

卑职不时巡视派驻日籍探员的各捕房，除检查日籍探员的工作日志外，还与负责的高级探员及巡官等协商，以确立受卑职监督的探员之间的工作协调和纪律。

除代表政治股、外籍股、华籍股、印籍股、军火股等部门调查案件（这往往伴随着困难和责任）外，卑职的职责还包括担任上海公共租界警务处与

REPORT ON THE NATURE OF DUTIES PERFORMED BY J.D.I. NAKAGAWA.

Made by J.D.I. S. Nakagawa Forwarded by

the Japanese authorities as well as the Japanese cotton
mills in the Eastern and Western districts.
In the case of serious crimes occurring in the Settlement
in which Japanese interests are involved or the service of
a Japanese Detective is indispensable, the undersigned is
invariably called upon to work in conjunction with the
senior foreign officer conducting the investigation.
It may not be amiss for me here to draw attention to the
fact that considerable care is being taken by the under-
signed to establish friendly relations between the Police
and the Japanese community at large and the officials in
particular in order to foster better understanding which is
essential for mutual co-operation. A connection of this
kind is of great value and facilitates enquiries.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

S. Nakagawa

REPORT ON INSTRUCTION CLASSES OF JAPANESE DETECTIVES

Made by J.G.Del. Nakagawa Forwarded by ____,

Sir,

With reference to the instructions contained in your memo dated June 1, 1929 referring to C. I. D. Conferences for Japanese Detectives, I beg respectfully to report that instruction classes have been held since May 3 on every Friday. Inasmuch as this system of instructing Detectives regularly has not formerly been in existence, all the Japanese Detectives, provided that the exigencies of the case permit, have been encouraged to attend the classes.

A summary of my lectures at each meeting is given below in chronological order in compliance with your orders:-

Friday, May 5:
Subjects dealt with.-
(1) Topography of Shanghai.
Explanations were given on the boundaries, situation, physical features, police districts, etc. of Shanghai.
(2) System of numbering of houses.
Differentiation of numbers on foreign and Chinese houses and the system of arranging the even and odd numbers on each side of the street as well as that of numbers increasing on one side of the street and decreasing on the other, the system common in the Settlement.
(3) Consular jurisdiction and how it affects C. I. D. work.

外国房屋与中国房屋号码的区别，以及街道两侧偶数和奇数排列的系统，还有租界内常见的一侧街道号码递增而另一侧递减的系统。
